subject: Media Literacy
title: Corrections and Accountability
description: A 60-second lesson on Corrections and Accountability.

hook.text: A newspaper publishes a false accusation on the front page. The correction appears six days later on page 14. Justice?

buildup.text: Ethical journalism requires publishing corrections when errors are discovered — promptly, prominently, and transparently.

discovery.text: Corrections demonstrate accountability. Outlets that correct errors openly are more trustworthy than those that quietly edit.

twist.text: Online media can silently edit articles without ever noting what changed. 'Stealth editing' erases the record of error.

climax.text: A correction buried or delayed does more damage than the original error. Accountability requires equal visibility.

punchline.text: A correction on page 14 doesn't fix a lie on page 1.

quiz.question: What is 'stealth editing' in online journalism?
options: Silently changing published articles without noting what was corrected
